events.title: Bronze Age islanders
events.text: The people of Borġ in-Nadur farm the land and guard their village with a stone wall above Marsaxlokk bay.

events.title: Ships from the east
events.text: Phoenician traders from Tyre's world begin to call at Malta's sheltered bays, halfway along their route west.

events.title: Shrine of Astarte
events.text: At Tas-Silġ, newcomers turn a ruined megalithic temple into a sanctuary of the goddess Astarte.

events.title: Maleth founded
events.text: Phoenician settlers occupy the Mdina plateau; their town is called Maleth, a name Rome will keep as Melite.

events.title: Neighbours at Baħrija
events.text: Phoenician pottery reaches the native hilltop village of Baħrija: islanders and newcomers trade and mix.

events.title: Rock-cut tombs
events.text: Families bury their dead in shaft tombs cut into the rock around Maleth, with jars, lamps and amulets.

events.title: Xlendi shipwreck
events.text: A Phoenician merchant ship sinks off Gozo with jars and grinding stones; divers find it in 2007, 110 metres down.

events.title: Gaulos on its hill
events.text: Settlers occupy the flat hilltop at the heart of Gozo, the future town of Gaulos.

events.title: Mtarfa burials
events.text: Phoenician tombs are cut into the ridge of Mtarfa, facing the new town across a valley.

events.title: Grand Harbour anchorage
events.text: Ships shelter at Marsa, at the head of the Grand Harbour, the largest natural port in the islands.

events.title: Channel crossing
events.text: Boats link Gozo and Malta across the narrow channel from the bay of Mġarr.

events.title: Tyre's long siege ends
events.text: Tyre submits to Babylon after a thirteen-year siege; in the west, Carthage takes the lead of the Phoenician colonies.

events.title: Carthage takes over
events.text: Over the sixth century BC, Malta and Gozo pass under the control of Carthage.

events.title: Punic Maleth
events.text: Maleth grows into a walled town, its houses and tomb-cut suburbs spreading over present-day Rabat.

events.title: Gaulos ruled from Carthage
events.text: Gozo's hilltop town becomes the Punic town of Gaulos.

events.title: A clay coffin
events.text: At Għar Barka in Rabat, the dead are laid in terracotta sarcophagi moulded with a human face, in Phoenician style.

events.title: Defeat at Himera
events.text: Carthage is beaten by the Greeks of Sicily; its hold on Malta, far to the south, is untouched.

events.title: Olive presses
events.text: A Punic farmstead at San Pawl Milqi presses olives above the Burmarrad plain.

events.title: Farms of Żejtun
events.text: Olive oil is pressed on a Punic farm where a Roman villa will later stand.

events.title: Offerings to Astarte
events.text: Pilgrims leave bowls inscribed in Punic for Astarte at the Tas-Silġ sanctuary.

events.title: Fields of Gozo
events.text: Punic farms spread across Gozo's plateaux, around Xagħra and Nadur.

events.title: Round towers
events.text: Round stone towers rise among the farms at Żurrieq, possibly as Punic lookouts.

events.title: Ta' Ċieda tower
events.text: A round tower at San Ġwann watches over the farms of the north coast.

events.title: Tyre falls
events.text: Alexander the Great storms Tyre, the mother city of the Phoenicians; Punic Malta looks only to Carthage.

events.title: Ras il-Wardija
events.text: A rock-cut Punic sanctuary is carved on Gozo's western cliffs, looking out over the sea.

events.title: Fine linen
events.text: Melite's weavers make linen famous for its fineness, as the Greek historian Diodorus later records.

events.title: War with Rome
events.text: The First Punic War begins in Sicily; Malta becomes Carthage's island base on the way to Sicily.

events.title: Rome builds a fleet
events.text: Rome wins its first sea battle at Mylae, and Carthage's islands are suddenly within reach.

events.title: Regulus raids Malta
events.text: The consul Gaius Atilius Regulus lands with a Roman army after his naval victory at Tyndaris.

events.title: The island burned
events.text: The poet Naevius, a veteran of the war, wrote that the Romans burned, plundered and laid waste the whole island.

events.title: Rebuilding
events.text: Carthage keeps Malta; farmers return to their burned estates.

events.title: Peace of Lutatius
events.text: Carthage loses Sicily but keeps Malta, now its front line facing Roman Sicily.

events.title: Carthage turns to Spain
events.text: After the Mercenary War, Hamilcar Barca leads Carthage's armies to Spain; Malta remains its outpost facing Sicily.

events.title: Hannibal marches
events.text: The Second Punic War begins; Carthage sends about two thousand soldiers to hold Malta.

events.title: Sempronius sails
events.text: The consul Tiberius Sempronius Longus sails from Lilybaeum in Sicily for Malta.

events.title: Hamilcar surrenders
events.text: Hamilcar son of Gisgo hands over the town and the island with almost two thousand soldiers, without a battle.

events.title: Sold as slaves
events.text: Except for men of noble birth, the captured garrison is sold into slavery.

events.title: Gozo becomes Roman
events.text: Gaulos passes to Rome with Malta; its Punic-speaking people stay.

chartNote: Share of the area of Malta and Gozo, by the dominant kind of settlement in each of today's local councils; the ancient islands had no such divisions. It is a simplification: the archaeology is patchy, dates are approximate, and the native islanders merged with the Phoenician newcomers.
